title: Could Spider-Man Really Turn Off His Powers?
summary:
Small movie spoilers ahead! In Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Peter Parker has problems caused by spider DNA from the bite that gave him powers. He wants to turn off some spider traits and keep others. Bruce Banner, who becomes the Hulk, has built a superpower inhibitor that could help.

The movie idea is based on real science. Tiny molecules called siRNAs can turn off certain genes. Genes are instructions in our DNA. Cells copy those instructions and use them to build proteins. An siRNA grabs a copy and marks it to be chopped up, so the protein is not made. Doctors already use at least eight siRNA treatments for diseases.

Scientist Anastasia Khvorova says siRNAs are good at shutting down foreign DNA, like spider DNA. But Peter wants to stop several different traits, so he would probably need a mix of siRNAs. Scientist Judy Lieberman says no one can control siRNAs that precisely yet.
why_it_matters: A superhero movie can help you learn how real medicine works inside your own body.
